chapter: Brown's Band and Tom in Chicago
title: Identifying Bakay and a bassist named Bro
summary: Brown cannot name Bakay's first name and suggests Chink; the interviewer asks about a bassist who knew him from Ellington's band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: I want to take two more things. What was Bakay's name? Do you remember? There was more than one of them here, I know.
And that's been so long ago, Gene.
Could it have been Ashiel or George or something like that? Could have been...
No, I couldn't help you out in that way.

Only way... I'll tell you. The only one that could help or answer that question would be Chink. He remembers Bakay and all those and could give you their first name more than I could, because he's been down in New Orleans more or less ever since. He left just for a short time up in Chicago and come right on back. So he remembered those names far more than I could.
Now another fellow... Did you ever know a fellow named Bro that played bass?
Well, he's from New Orleans, but he was with Duke Ellington for a while. And he traveled all over with Ellington. Bro, no.
I don't imagine so. He was evidently a young kid when I was gone. No, I was about your...
In 192, he was born in 192, about two years younger.

Wellman Bro, he said he played with Duke Ellington. He said you were his favorite bass player. Yeah, I told him that last month. He said you were the greatest bass player I ever heard. Well, maybe... You'd know him if you saw him, I'm sure. I think so. You'd know him if you saw him.
